_comment: Running list of player-facing patch notes for the NEXT release. As work ships, append entries here. The patch-notes skill rolls this into Assets/data/patchnotes.json on release and clears pending. Categories: feature, balance, fix, polish, content.

entries.line: Five new beasts join the Beastbook (#16–20): Gnoll → Gnollium (a forest gnome line drawn from European hidden-folk myth), Jackacabra (a chupacabra-hare shadow predator that slips into Weaverton's pastures at dusk to raid the Sheepot flocks), and Padlip → Liliprince (a frog-prince line based on the Brothers Grimm tale — Water until the curse breaks, then Water/Spirit). All five by Jet.

Region identity pass — the three launch zones now share a single story. Saltmoor Cove → Weaverton, the wool-and-loom village built around the Sheepot trade. The Witherwood → Weaverwood, the dye-leaf forest east of town where the herders take their flocks each summer. Old Saltmoor → Weavermere, the mirror-still pond above Weaverton where the village's painters and dye-masters chase the colors no loom can match.

AI-generated wild beasts retired pre-launch — the Beastbook is now a tighter, all-handmade roster. The starter pool, the Weaverwood, and the Weavermere now spawn only handmade species (the old AI-gen beasts still exist in the species DB so prior contracts don't break, just hidden from the book).

Weaverwood (Lv 10) is now the Gnoll/Jackacabra hunting ground — Gnoll spawns wild, Jackacabra prowls the wood's edge raiding Sheepot flocks, and Wishlift + Twincoil drift in from the village pasture. Gnollium is evo-only or boss-roll; Liliprince is boss-only at Weavermere.

Side quests + trade nodes retuned around the new handmade roster — the Weaverwood now offers a Jackacabra cull bounty, a Gnollcap tribute, a Twincoil weave, and the Weavermere's three artist NPCs (Painter Selene, Dye-Master Wren, the Wandering Poet) trade Padlip pondlight motes for relics, dye recipes, and verses.

Beastbook grid no longer stretches non-square monster art — Seraphiel and Aurael, whose source canvases are wider than they are tall, are now rendered at proper proportion instead of being squashed/stretched into a 180x180 box. Aurael in particular shows much more wing/halo/blade detail.

Day 7 streak reward swapped from a Legendary beast to a Master Ink — guaranteed contract on your next attempt. The legendary tier isn't live in open beta yet, so the old reward couldn't actually be granted in any meaningful form.

Beastbook #1–19 balance pass — growth rates raised across the launch roster so beasts level up faster, BSTs reined in to fit their rarity bands (Gnoll/Gnollium/Padlip trimmed, Liliprince pushed up to Rare-tier parity), Jackacabra contract rate eased to 0.35. Jackacabra now learns a signature move Goatsucker's Drain (Lv 38) — heals for 50% of damage dealt — and Liliprince learns a signature Sovereign's Boon (Lv 55) — 90-power Spirit special that heals the caster 25%.

Five new flavor signature moves for Beastbook #10–14: Sheepot learns Pot Guard (Lv 21, raises DEF + SpD), Cerametz learns Solstice Veil (Lv 38, heals 33% wrapped in solstice fleece), Wishlift learns Dream Drift (Lv 19, drifts a spent-wish bubble across the foe's eyes for sleep), Twincoil learns Two-Faced Strike (Lv 19, the outer head bites + the inner head hexes, guaranteed -1 ATK), and Heartwell learns Inner Stillness (Lv 21, the sokushinbutsu monk's meditation — heals 33% and cleanses status). Gothsire's late movelist also retuned: whirlpool_surge moved to Lv 40 as a proper Water capstone, current_boost slid down to Lv 26 where it actually gets used.

Embark popup completely redesigned in the Persona-stamp battle-UI dialect — team slots now show big sprite art carved into a diagonal slab on the left, italic-skewed display name on the right, gold Lv pill, gold-edged element badges, and a prominent HP bar. Reads as a sibling of the battle nameplates instead of a generic list row.

Embark popup roster now actually fits 5+ beasts per row at full card size — was previously clipping the 5th card on a row of 4 due to a stack of three engine quirks (a transformed ancestor, a ghost hover-scale on the cards, and a stale `overflow: hidden` on the world map container) that all conspired to collapse the available width. Layout's been rebuilt to dodge all three.

Embark popup no longer teleports from the top-left to the center on open. The entrance animation was authored back when the modal centered via a transform offset; switching to flex-centering left the offset stuck on the keyframes, sending the modal to the corner for 0.22s before it snapped back.

Wishlift gains an evolution — Wishstar (#13, Wind/Spirit, Rare). When a Wishlift carries enough wishes home the wishes outweigh her, and what falls out the other side is a king with a planet for a body and a sun for a crown — each continent etched across him is a dream that found its way back. Evolves at Lv 32. Art by Spookior.
Achievement descriptions now use 'Contract' terminology throughout — 'Contract your first monster', 'Contract 100 monsters', etc. — consistent with the rest of the game.
Removed loyalty references from UI to match current design (loyalty system was retired pre-launch).
Fixed Branchling's description, which contained unfilled template placeholders from an earlier data pass.
Achievement panel and Shop now use the Persona-stamp dialect on their hero CTAs (Claim All / Buy buttons) and titles.
Mini-expeditions added — short optional adventures that branch off the main path and offer exclusive rewards. The first one unlocks after clearing Weavermere.
Tuned XP yields across the launch roster — wild encounters now grant XP appropriate to their rarity and evolution stage.
Rarity bands rebalanced — Epic now sits properly above Rare in the stat ladder. A new beast line lands in the new Epic band, waiting somewhere off the path above Weavermere.
New beast line added — descend into a hidden mini-expedition near Weavermere to find them.
Whispering Hollow mini-expedition marker tooltip no longer clips off the left map edge — tooltip now anchors to the right of the pin instead of above it.

Clicking a mini-expedition on the world map now opens a full detail panel (drops, beasts, level, waves, boss) before you embark — same flow as main zones. Loomweaver's detail card shows a 'Cannot Contract' tag since it's evo-only.
Whispering Hollow now hosts a varied wild pool — Threadlet shares the cave with Cerametz, Twincoil, and Wishlift.
Threadlet now appears as a rarer wild encounter in Whispering Hollow.
Removed an empty Adventure Wave radio station entry — expedition music context is reserved and will be filled when tracks are ready.

Battle status indicators redesigned with clearer icons and color coding — Burn, Freeze, Paralyze, Poison, Sleep, and Confuse each have a distinct icon and tinted badge instead of generic emoji glyphs. Breeding panel egg icon updated to match the game's icon style.

Burn and Poison hit harder — Burn now ticks for 1/15 of MaxHP per turn (was 1/20) and Poison ticks for 1/10 (was 1/12). Status conditions are meaningful pressure again, especially in longer boss fights.
Internal save migration cleanup — minor save-load speedup.
Threadlet line text polish — clearer signature move descriptions and a small description tune.
Evolutions now play a proper transformation sound instead of a generic UI click.
Cleaned up unused leaderboard categories that weren't surfacing meaningful data.

Guild officers with pending join requests can now actually see them — the Invite button correctly opens the join requests list when requests are pending, instead of always jumping to the invite-player picker. The Invite Player option is still accessible via a button inside the requests panel.

Pending guild join requests panel refreshed — stamped title, bordered request cards with left accent and stagger entrance animation, ACCEPT/DENY buttons in the Beastborne dialect, and time-since timestamps replacing the stale ranked RP display.

Invite Player picker refreshed — header icon, close button, online indicator dot, level badge for offline friends, and empty-state messaging. Both the picker and the requests panel now share the same card chrome (dark solid border, offset purple drop shadow).
Guild invites can now reach friends you've previously played with — not just tamers in your current lobby. Online friends show a green dot; offline friends show their level.
Dewdrop joins the handmade roster — a small round waterdrop with a single leaf for a cap, now Water/Nature dual-typed. Drifts across Weavermere alongside Padlip and the other pond wilds. Art by Jet.

Main-menu → game transition rebuilt — a Persona-style diagonal wipe: gold and purple slabs sweep in to cover the screen, the mascot and BEASTBORNE wordmark stamp over the seam, then the slabs split open to reveal your Hub. (The old transition stopped animating after the engine update.)

Dewdrop now evolves — Duodew (#24, Water/Nature, Uncommon) at Lv 30. The drop that found water still enough to never leave: it roots into the pond floor, raises a leaf overhead like a parasol, and tends a second little drop at its side — the next Dewdrop, not ready to drift. Learns a signature move, Wellspring Surge (Lv 34): a 90-power Water special that heals it for 25% of the damage dealt. Art by Jet.

Stomplet → Skunkape — a new bigfoot shepherd line walks the Weaverwood. Stomplet is the young leafy giant who tends the Sheepot flocks; Skunkape is the elder, mossy and leaf-crowned. Contract a Stomplet in the forest and evolve it at Lv 32. Art by Jet.

Repaired expedition achievement milestones — 'Clear all expeditions' (Conqueror) now actually unlocks at 3 zones cleared instead of 16, and the Weaverwood and Weavermere step achievements now trigger correctly. Hard Mode equivalents fixed to match.
Skunkape's Beastbook evolution chain now correctly shows Stomplet as its pre-evolution.
Skill tree SP counter now just shows your available skill points instead of a confusing X / total fraction. The number is the SP you have to spend, no hidden cap.

Element colors normalized — Nature is consistently emerald-green, Wind is consistently teal. Pills, gradients, borders, badges, move buttons, and the battle UI now match their element icons across every panel.

Burn, Poison, Paralyze, and Freeze status effects now actually persist turn-over-turn instead of self-clearing after a single tick. The recent status damage buff (Burn 1/15, Poison 1/10) now delivers as designed.
Fixed a buggy evolution-upgrade entry on the Duskstalker line that had Umbral Claw evolving into itself — harmless no-op cleaned up.
Pollen Burst now actually does what its description says — 10% chance to poison the target, in line with other Nature/toxin moves.
Dual-type beasts (Dewdrop, Cerametz, Wishstar, Liliprince, Manehelm, Lochmaw, Twincoil, Loomweaver) now show both element badges in the roster and team-picker card views, not just their primary type.
Loomweaver's Beastbook entry now shows a 'Cannot Contract' badge alongside its rarity — it's evolution-only, so this was previously missing context for players who found it in the book.

Stomplet and Skunkape rebalanced into proper Uncommon and Rare bands. Stomplet picks up Sapling Stomp at Lv 21 (60-power Nature physical that hardens the user's stance). Skunkape gets Shepherd's Vigil at Lv 55 (90-power Nature special that pulls life back into the caster).

Dewdrop's moveset refreshed to match its identity — rebuilt around a leaf-capped waterdrop bobbing on still ponds at dawn. Dropped the off-brand ocean/striking moves (no limbs, no surf), traded for pond-mist Water specials (Tidal Pulse, Waterlog, Monsoon Call, Deep Pressure), dawn-light Spirit moves (Spirit Breeze, Aether Pulse), a dawn-mist Wind shield (Gust Shield Lv 22), and the new signature Leafcap Drift at Lv 28 (50-power Nature special, 30% to put the foe to sleep — the leaf-cap dipping forward and the pondsteam doing the rest).

Roster-wide moveset lore audit — every learnable move now has a clear reason that specific beast would know it. Wishlift sheds claw and tackle moves she doesn't have (she drifts on dream-bubbles, not pounces) and picks up Spirit Breeze + Aether Pulse for the dream-light fae flavor. Heartwell, the sokushinbutsu monk under the village fountain, drops his striking moves for the calm vow they belie — gains Aether Pulse (the patient pulse that always lands) and Deep Pressure (the well's settled weight). Padlip the pondfrog sheds ocean-flavored moves (he lives in lily-pads, not the sea) and picks up Tidal Pulse for the throat-sac vibration plus Aqua Shield for the bubble around his body. Cherune the novice cherub trades a feint-jab for Spirit Breeze — guardians leave warmth, not stings.

Heartwell and Twincoil — both standalone Commons that never evolve — got a stat-band lift toward the middle of their tier. Heartwell (BST 267 → 297) leans deeper into the sokushinbutsu monk's identity with more HP and SpD; the well's weight is harder to disturb now. Twincoil (BST 263 → 290) gains a touch more bite and serpentine quickness across the board. Both feel viable into mid-game instead of falling off the moment the player's starter mid-evolves.

Trait pills now show a unique icon per trait — Kindle Heart gets a campfire, Phantom Step gets footprints, Trickster gets a masquerade mask, Lightning Rod gets an antenna, and so on across the full 38-trait roster.

Strict moveset lore pass across the full launch roster — every learnable move now defends itself against the beast's specific identity. Timid beasts stopped learning Intimidate (Sheepot, Pagefin, Stomplet, Wishlift, Cherune); brooding-loyal beasts stopped 'wrath' and 'annihilate' moves that clashed with their patience (Cerametz, Gnollium, Skunkape, Manehelm sentinel); freshwater pond-monks stopped saltwater 'brine/sea/tidal-ward' moves (Heartwell, Liliprince); a king who sleeps standing stopped learning Agility Boost and Tornado Dive (Wishstar); a TIMID flame-foal stopped war-crying (Embrik). Replacements stay in-pool but lean into each beast's actual description — Sheepot picks up Parasite Spore for its fragile-root underside, Skunkape's elder-shepherd kit gets Bloom Burst / Verdant Edge / Overgrowth Slam instead of generic 'crushing/vicious/annihilate' verbs, Wishstar gains Calm Air to match its standing-sleep, Heartwell picks up Warding Hymn + Spirit Link for the monk's vows, and Cherune gets Luminous Wall + Aether Pulse for the guardian-cherub identity that awakens fully at evolution. Dewdrop's Nature dual-typing gets a light touch — the leaf-cap learns Nature Shield (Lv 20, the leaf curls over the drop) and Blade Leaf (Lv 23, leaf-flick edge) on top of the existing Leafcap Drift signature, while keeping its sturdy pond-water core intact.

Hard Mode unlocked per-expedition — clear an expedition on Normal to unlock its Hard variant. Tougher fights (+25% enemy levels, +15% ATK/SpA, +10% HP/DEF/SpD, speed unchanged), bigger rewards (2× XP, 2× gold, 1.5× drop rate), and a zone-specific Hard Token currency awarded on clear — Tide Tokens from Weaverton, Loom Tokens from Weaverwood, Dawn Tokens from Weavermere, Threaded Tokens from Whispering Hollow. Each zone tracks Hard unlock and first-Hard-clear independently.

Expedition team selection now shows a NORMAL / HARD difficulty toggle before you embark. Hard mode (once unlocked for that zone) turns the BEGIN EXPEDITION button red and shows a small HARD MODE kicker above it.

If the save server is unreachable on a machine with no local backup, you're now shown a clear prompt with Retry and Play Offline options instead of silently starting a fresh save that could overwrite your real cloud save on reconnect.

Help tab refreshed — status effect tick rates and persistence updated (Burn 1/15 MaxHP, Poison 1/10 MaxHP, both persist until healed), Whispering Hollow mini-expedition added to the Zones section, dual-type beast list added to the Elements section, Online Hub section updated to reflect the 3-tab launch layout, and Contract/Beastbook terminology cleaned throughout.
Auto-Battler UI and code removed — the feature was scope-cut and the leftover plumbing was dead weight.

Contract encounter UI polish — the radial panel now shows a gold 'CONTRACT · LV X' kicker above the creature sprite, the diamond frame switches to an element-tinted border instead of a flat background fill, and the approach-match indicator uses a cleaner star icon.

Fusion Complete reveal redesigned — result now appears in a 3-stage cinematic sequence: dark wash → beast portrait slides in with its species name → gene table drops in showing each stat vs both parents (green if better than average, red if worse). Two CTAs replace the old Continue button: 'VIEW BEAST' (gold border, routes to your roster) and 'FUSE AGAIN' (ghost, returns to parent picker).
Tamer Card 'Share in Chat' button now plays a sound and shows a toast confirmation when clicked — previously the card was being posted but there was no feedback so it felt broken.

Tutorial walkthrough refreshed for the current game — contract approach count corrected (four approaches, not twelve), Hard Mode mentioned in the closing step, and winning or losing an expedition now plays a victory or defeat sound instead of silence.

Hit-flash on damage taken — sprites now snap to a single bright-white flash for 80ms when struck, instead of the old 400ms red-flicker that dragged across the camera shake. Fighting-game-tight; hits actually feel like hits now.
KO collapse — when a beast faints it now slumps forward 25° while dropping, instead of just translating straight down. Reads as a knocked-out monster rather than a teleport-out.

Status conditions now show ambient halos on the sprite in battle, not just an icon on the nameplate. Burn flickers orange, Poison pulses purple, Paralyze zaps yellow every couple seconds, Freeze sits in a still cyan wash, Sleep breathes slow blue, and Confuse wobbles pink. You can read what's on a beast from across the screen.
Chat, Radio, Active Effects, and Notifications popups can now be dragged anywhere on screen — grab the header to reposition. Each popup remembers where you moved it between sessions.
Toast notifications no longer reappear after you dismiss them — they stay gone until a new one arrives.
Beast descriptions tightened — every launch beast now reads as a clean 1-2 sentence identity instead of a paragraph.
Trade request popup upgraded — lucide swap icon, gold italic 'TRADE REQUEST' kicker, and canonical Accept/Decline button styles.

Move selection panel refreshed — category icons (Physical/Special/Status) are now lucide icons in a counter-rotated diamond badge; PWR, PP, and ACC shown as distinct labeled pills; SWAP uses a lucide refresh icon.
Swap panel polish — each monster card now shows a 3px rarity-color strip at the bottom and an element-tinted border rim so you can read rarity and type at a glance.

Beast Showcase popup upgraded — close button uses a proper icon, the veteran badge uses a lucide medal, and stats are now shown as a 6-bar visual grid (HP/ATK/DEF/SpA/SpD/SPD) with color-coded fills, matching the Beastbook.
Expedition popup upgraded — swords icon, gold italic 'IN PROGRESS' kicker above the zone name, and VIEW/END buttons now show lucide icons alongside their labels.

Battles are now fully keyboard-playable — arrow keys move between FIGHT/SWITCH/BAG/CONTRACT/END, number keys 1-4 instantly fire a move, 1-3 pick a target, Q swaps and E opens the bag, Space confirms and Shift backs out. Every action and move shows its hotkey on a small key-cap right on the label. Mouse still works exactly as before.

Menus and popups are now keyboard-navigable too — arrow keys move the highlight, Space confirms, Shift backs out. Confirm dialogs, the menu popup, options, the shop, the world map, and the expedition result screen can all be driven without the mouse. Opening a popup hands it the keyboard so it never fights the screen underneath it.
Hard Mode can now actually be selected on the expedition team screen — the HARD pill showed as unlocked but clicking it only played a deny sound.
Beast gene totals were undercounting — the roster GENES value and gene-sort now count all six genes (Sp. Atk and Sp. Def were being left out).
Boss reward drops no longer include catch lures — catch items are shop-only.
Beasts revived between expedition waves no longer occasionally come back tilted from their KO collapse.
Confirming CONTRACT with the keyboard during battle no longer activates END instead — keyboard selection now always matches the highlighted action diamond.

Breeding panel now shows all six genes — the parent comparison table and the offspring gene-range preview were missing Sp. Atk and Sp. Def, and the gene-total cap read /200 instead of the correct /180.

Daily milestone rewards now unlock by total cumulative login days as intended — the claim button was wrongly gated on the consecutive streak, so anyone who missed a day could never claim the longer milestones even with the progress bar full.
The 'Supreme Tamer' achievement no longer unlocks early — it now correctly requires defeating all three expedition bosses, including the Loomweaver's Burrow mini-expedition boss.
Chat popup now moves smoothly while you drag it — previously the window only snapped to its new position when some unrelated update (a new message, a channel switch) happened to refresh the panel.
Game tabs now switch only with the number keys 1-6 — pressing WASD or the arrow keys no longer jumps you between tabs, so those keys stop interfering with panel and content navigation.

The bag is now fully keyboard-navigable — number keys 1-7 switch category tabs, WASD or arrows move the item cursor, Space uses the highlighted item, and Q closes the bag. The bag was also widened so the item grid fits comfortably.
The contract negotiation screen is now keyboard-navigable — 1-4 pick an approach, A/D step between them, Space attempts the contract, Tab toggles Master Ink, and Q cancels.
Help tab gains a Controls section — a full keyboard guide covering tab navigation, battle, taming, the bag, and popups so the keyboard map is discoverable in-game.
Keyboard 'confirm' across menus, battle, and popups is now consistently Space or Enter — it was previously also bound to the left mouse button action, which could double-fire a click.

Beasts roster keyboard navigation fixed — the detail panel now follows your keyboard selection instead of flickering the whole grid on every keypress, and W/S move exactly one row (they were jumping a fixed 5 cards regardless of how many actually fit per row).

Roster and Beastbook detail panels are now fully keyboard-operable — press Space on a beast to hand keyboard control to the detail panel, where the arrows move a cursor over every interactive control (the nickname pencil, the showcase/journal/favourite diamonds, the action buttons, and all four move slots in the Beasts panel). Space activates the highlighted control, the panel auto-scrolls to keep it on screen, and Q returns to the grid.

The bottom command bar's non-tab buttons now have keyboard shortcuts — 7 opens Quests, 8 the Menu, 9 the Bag, 0 your Profile, and T/R/C/N toggle Chat, Radio, Active Effects, and Notifications. Each button shows its key on a small gold key-cap, matching the 1-6 tab caps.

The in-game guide is now fully keyboard-navigable — W/S (or arrows) walk a single cursor through every topic and sub-page in one list, and the guide updates live as you move. Space starts reading (W/S then scroll the page), and Q steps back to the list, then closes the guide. The Controls section also now renders correctly — it was previously showing a blank page.
Beastbook keyboard navigation — W/S now move exactly one row instead of jumping a fixed 8 cards; the row size is measured from the live grid so it stays correct at any window width.

Shop keyboard navigation no longer jumps between categories — A/D and W/S now follow the on-screen order (the grid regroups items by category, but navigation had been walking the raw unsorted list), and W/S move to the item directly above or below across category section breaks.
Keyboard navigation in the My Beasts roster, Beastbook, and Shop now scrolls the grid to follow your selection — the highlighted card stays on screen instead of drifting out of view as you move.

The Embark / team-picker popup is now fully keyboard-operable — arrows or WASD move a visible cursor through your roster (it scrolls to follow), Space/Enter picks a beast, F auto-fills, C clears, 1/2/3 load or save team presets, the < and > keys cycle the element filter, R embarks and Q closes. Every action button shows its key on a small gold cap.
Heartwell's sprite refreshed with cleaner, updated art.

Full-roster moveset lore pass — one more sweep so every beast's moveset reads true to its body and personality. Embrik, the timid headless flame-foal with no claws, trades a 'brutal slash' for Cinder's Curse (its hollow ghost-flame). Pyrgard and Manehelm, loyal protector-knights, stop war-crying — they steel themselves with Forge Temper instead, and Manehelm swaps a 'primal roar' for an Ember Wall guard befitting a sentinel. Seraphiel, Aurael, and Wishstar drop wind 'talon/claw' moves they have no talons for (a serpent-armed seraph, a phantom-handed herald, a planet-bodied king) and pick up clean wind-cut and wind-slam moves instead. Liliprince the Weavermere pond-prince sheds an ocean-energy ward for a freshwater Aqua Shield. Lochmaw the deep-sea apex predator stops bracing and learns Dread Gaze — the deep waters part before it. Cerametz, the patient urn-sheep, stops going into a self-confusing Blossom Frenzy and lashes out with Wild Thorn instead.

Off-element move pass — beasts whose stories reach beyond their element now learn a move to match. Embrik, a foal born dead and animated by a borrowed flame, picks up the shadowy Shade Step. Pyrgard's forged burning helm gives it the steel-hard Iron Rush, foreshadowing Manehelm's Fire/Metal typing. Brooding dark-knight Gothsire learns the shadow-clawed Umbral Claw, foreshadowing Lochmaw's Water/Shadow turn. The warden-seraph Seraphiel blesses its silvered blade with Sacred Strike, and the crowned herald Aurael calls down Lunar Radiance — Spirit moves for an angelic line. And Twincoil's hexing inner face, the one whose eyes never blink, learns Dread Gaze.

The 'Perfection' achievement (fuse a beast with a perfect gene) can now actually be earned — it was checking for a gene value of 31, which is impossible since genes cap at 30, so the achievement was permanently unreachable.

The 'Beastborne Master' achievement (discover every species) no longer counts the retired AI-gen beasts that are hidden from the Beastbook and can't be encountered — completion now correctly tracks the handmade launch roster. The Beastbook completion counter and percentage display were also reading against the full hidden roster and now show the right numbers.

Fixed achievement rewards being silently lost — if you unlocked an achievement and quit before claiming it, the next login would mark it claimed without ever granting the reward. Unclaimed achievement rewards now reliably wait for you.
Boss-clear achievements ('Boss Slayer', 'Supreme Tamer') now unlock retroactively for players who defeated expedition bosses before these achievements existed.

The 'Point Hoarder' achievement (invest 100 skill points) now counts skill-point cost correctly when checking past progress — skills that cost more than 1 point per rank were being undercounted, so the achievement could fail to unlock for players who had genuinely spent enough.

Hard Mode expedition achievements reworded to match what they actually track — they unlock on the number of expeditions cleared on Hard Mode, in any order, so they're now 'Clear 1/2/3 expeditions on Hard Mode' (Hard Mode Initiate / Veteran / Master) instead of naming specific zones, which could mislead.

Shop Daily Spotlight card no longer shows the level-requirement lock floating loose under the discount badge — the lock now sits as a clean stacked pair directly beneath the '% OFF TODAY' badge, properly aligned and spaced.
Shop Daily Spotlight card's vertical divider hairline renders correctly again — a gradient quirk had collapsed it to an invisible sliver.
Radio widget's progress bar no longer overlaps the now-playing track card — it now sits below the card with a clean gap.

The Online tab is now keyboard-navigable — the < and > keys cycle between the Tamers, Leaderboards, and Guild sections, arrows or WASD move a cursor through the tamer tiles, Space/Enter opens a tamer's card in the sidebar, and the grid scrolls to keep your selection on screen.

The main menu is now fully keyboard-operable end to end — the open-beta greeting, the Now Hiring popup, the cloud-save-unreachable prompt, and the reset-data confirm all take the keyboard while open (arrows pick a button, Space confirms, Q backs out to the safe choice), and the Patch Notes panel scrolls with the arrow keys or the mouse wheel.

The Skill tree is now keyboard-navigable — WASD or arrows move a gold cursor between skill nodes (it picks the nearest node in whatever direction you press), Space invests in the focused node, Tab swaps between the TREE and STATS views, and F triggers the reset button. The focused node shows its full tooltip so you can read cost and effect before investing.

On-screen hotkey hints added across more panels — the Skill tree shows a 'Tab' cap for switching the TREE/STATS views and an 'F' cap on the reset button, and the Online hub, Shop, and Beastbook each show a '< >' hint for the keys that cycle sections, stores, and the element filter.
Cycling a panel's sections/stores/element filter no longer also skips the radio track — panel cycling moved to the < and > keys, leaving [ and ] as the dedicated radio track-skip shortcut.

Loading your save no longer falsely claims that offline progress was discarded on every boot — and when your local progress is more recent than the cloud (e.g. the last cloud sync didn't finish before you closed the game), that newer progress is now kept and synced up, instead of being silently replaced by a slightly older cloud copy.

The Leaderboards tab is now keyboard-navigable — A/D rotate the category-group carousel (Battle, Collection, Social, Economy), W/S move a cursor through the category cards, Space expands the focused card to the top 20, and F refreshes the boards.

The Guild panel is now fully keyboard-navigable — every view (landing, browse, the guild plaza, and the create-guild form) can be driven without the mouse. WASD or arrows move a cursor and Space confirms; in the guild plaza W/S flow straight down the whole screen — action tiles, announcement/description cards, roster, perks, danger zone — and A/D move sideways within a section. The Announcement and Description edit pencils and the full Guild Settings drawer are all keyboard-operable — arrows walk the setting rows, left/right or Space changes each one. The browse grid, perk list, and settings drawer scroll to keep your selection on screen, and every sub-panel — the member context menu, join-requests list, invite picker, and raid team select — takes the keyboard while open. Q backs out.

The bag's ALL ITEMS count now matches the items actually shown — old saves could carry ghost item IDs (typo'd daily-streak rewards like 'gene_booster' that should have been 'boss_gene_booster', plus stale material IDs from removed beasts) that inflated the badge total but never rendered. The header now filters to only items that can resolve, and the typo'd milestone reward IDs are corrected so future grants resolve to real items. Unresolvable IDs are kept in your save (not deleted) so that if a future patch adds the missing registration, those items reappear.

Fixed the entire UI rendering at the wrong size after the s&box 26.06.03 engine update — the CSS engine changed unitless line-height to a font-size multiplier, which ballooned every text element's line box and shoved the menu and panels out of place. All line-heights pinned to explicit pixel values; menus, battle, roster, shop, and every panel lay out correctly again.

Skill tree no longer drifts out of sync across sessions — a self-healing audit now runs on every login, level-up, and shop reset and quietly puts your skill points and invested ranks back in step if any prior corruption left them mismatched. The shop's 'Respec' button now also refunds the full cost-correct SP and actually clears the tree (the old respec was clearing a throwaway list and refunding only one rank per skill, regardless of how much you'd invested). Trees that were already healthy are left alone — no surprise wipes.

Fusion Complete is now a proper cinematic moment — the screen dims while a charge ring spins up, then a flash blooms as your new beast slams in on a column of light with its name. The gene table cascades in row by row showing each stat against both parents, and the quality and nature settle in last. The fuse payoff finally feels earned, not flat.

Signing a contract now lands like the catch it is — the 'Contract Signed!' panel slams in with a flash, the title punches in, and your new beast springs up from a burst of light and sparks instead of just fading on screen. The four approach diamonds also fan in left-to-right each time the contract screen opens.

Claiming an achievement reward now actually celebrates — a gold flash, an expanding shockwave ring, a 12-mote sparkle burst, and a center card that slams in naming what you earned, all timed so your currency ticks up right as the burst peaks. Claim All gets the same moment with a running count. The achievement list also now cascades in row by row each time you open the panel or switch categories instead of appearing all at once.

Claiming your Day 7 streak reward is now a full-screen moment — the room dims and an iris ring contracts, then your Master Ink slams up a pillar of light, a gold-and-purple name banner punches in with god-rays and confetti, and your currency ticks up right as the celebration peaks. Routine daily claims stay quick and snappy, so the seventh day actually feels like the payoff it is.

Expedition screen feels like an event now — the team-select view assembles itself with a staggered slide-in (header, then roster, then your team panel cascading top to bottom) every time you open it, and clearing a zone fires a green 'ZONE CLEARED' burst with a light-ray sweep and expanding spark ring before the rewards screen lands.

Arena win screens now celebrate the big moments — climbing a rank tier fires a gold 'RANK UP' flash with your old rank arrowing up into the new one, and hitting a win-streak milestone (3, 5, 10, 15+) drops a full-screen moment: the screen dims, god-rays and shockwaves bloom, and your streak number slams in flanked by flames. Earned through wins, not luck.

Completing a trade now lands like a real exchange — a green flash, twin shockwave rings, a sparkle burst, and rotating light-rays bloom behind a 'TRADE COMPLETE' card that slams in, with a layered success-and-reward chime. The incoming trade-request popup also got a polish pass: its gold icon spins in, the title/message/buttons stagger up, and the Accept/Decline buttons now press in when you click them.

Discovering a new species now gets a proper moment in the Beastbook — when you contract a beast you've never recorded, a full-screen 'NEW SPECIES DISCOVERED' reveal blooms: the screen dims, light rings and rays sweep out behind the beast as it springs in, and its name slams up with a sparkle burst, tinted to its rarity. The Beastbook grid also deals its cards in on open, and selecting a beast now cascades its detail page into view instead of snapping.

Main menu rebuilt as a launcher hub — a frosted left sidebar (logo, big gold PLAY block, Roadmap/Options/Patch Notes nav, Discord card) alongside a featured update card with live event pill, headline art, and quick Roadmap/Community shortcuts. Reads like a live-service launcher and surfaces what's new the moment you boot.

Main menu color + life pass — the featured card now reads as a raised, lit-from-above surface with a breathing rim glow, the PLAY button carries a slow gold sheen and breathing halo to draw the eye, and the Roadmap and Community cards each picked up their own identity (teal-blue for Roadmap, Discord blurple for Community) with a glowing accent edge and lift on hover. The OUT NOW stamp wiggles, the purple backdrop drifts, and the whole menu feels alive instead of flat.

Main menu no longer shows two things lit at once — when you switch from the mouse to the keyboard, the Play Now / Patch Notes buttons and the Roadmap/Community cards drop their mouse-hover glow immediately, leaving only the keyboard selection. Move the mouse and hover comes right back.

Main menu keyboard navigation is now fully 2D — WASD (or arrows) move the violet selection in every direction, so you can press D from the sidebar to reach the Play Now / Patch Notes buttons and the Roadmap / Community cards on the right, which were previously unreachable by keyboard. LANGUAGE and QUIT now sit as a left/right pair (D goes to QUIT, A back to LANGUAGE).

Main menu Roadmap & Community cards redesigned — instead of repeating the sidebar, the Roadmap card now previews what's in development (Tower Mode, Ranked Battling) and the Community card shows live Discord presence with the real member count pulled straight from Discord.

Roadmap popup redesigned as 'What We're Building' — a clean 3×2 grid of feature cards (Tower Mode and Ranked Battling marked IN DEVELOPMENT with a violet accent, the rest COMING UP), a live OPEN BETA status pill, and a footer that invites you to send feedback or join the Discord.

Main menu now renders in the game's italic display type throughout — titles, nav, and body copy all carry the Beastborne slant (the italic font face is now actually loaded in-engine instead of silently falling back to upright).

Open-beta welcome popup redesigned to match the refined menu — a two-line title, flask icon badge, cleaner copy that invites suggestions, improvements, and feature ideas (not just bug reports), a single Got It button with a violet focus ring, and a smooth pop-up / pop-down animation. The Roadmap popup's Send Feedback button now opens the in-game feedback panel.
Main menu selection is now a single 'living' cursor — one violet ring that glides and liquid-stretches between options as you hover or arrow around, instead of each option lighting up in place.

Main menu right panel cleanup — the Community card's Join button and divider line no longer get clipped off the right edge, and the featured Update card's right edge now lines up flush with the Roadmap/Community cards below it on a matching angle (it previously leaned in steeper since it's a wider card).

Main menu now tilts into the screen for real depth — the sidebar buttons, the featured Update card, and the Roadmap/Community cards all recede on a consistent 3D angle, with the two bottom cards reading as one continuous receding surface.

Selecting a sidebar option (Roadmap / Options / Patch Notes) now fills it with a deep-violet highlight behind the label, ringed by the brighter living cursor — and the fill has a gentle liquid motion of its own that plays against the ring, so the selection feels alive.

Main menu has a brand-new animated wave background — a custom looping animation now fills the whole backdrop, replacing the old static pattern, the faint purple bokeh video, and the drifting light beam.
